options.metric: Annual number of motorists killed in reported crashes
options.reason: A fatality count is the most direct measure of the annual motorist death burden available in this file.
options.answer: The file records 110 motorists killed in 2013 and 81 in 2025 (a 26% decrease), but without miles driven it cannot establish whether deaths per mile declined.
options.interpretation: This framing addresses whether the observed motorist death count fell between the endpoints, and the chart shows a decline from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025. A count is a defensible measure of fatality burden, but it does not adjust for travel exposure and therefore leaves deaths per mile unanswered.

options.denominator: All police-reported crashes in the same year
options.reason: Normalizing deaths by recorded crashes provides a crash-severity comparison when travel-distance exposure is unavailable.
options.answer: Motorist deaths per 100,000 reported crashes rose from 54.0 in 2013 to 94.7 in 2025 (a 75% increase), but this is not a per-mile risk measure and cannot answer whether deaths per mile declined.
options.interpretation: This framing examines deaths relative to crash volume; its chart shows an increase from 54.0 deaths per 100,000 crashes in 2013 to 94.7 in 2025. It is a defensible crash-normalized proxy, but reported crashes are not vehicle miles traveled, so it leaves per-mile risk unanswered.
